title: Sixth Word Applying The Comparison Selling The Trust

questions.question: In the parable, who does the king stand for?
questions.answer: He stands for Allah, the Lord and Creator who has no beginning or end.

questions.question: What do the estate, equipment, and measuring tools represent in a person’s real life?
questions.answer: They represent a person’s belongings and also the body, soul, heart, and different abilities and senses.

questions.question: Which two things in the parable are explained as the noble lieutenant and the decree?
questions.answer: The lieutenant stands for the Messenger of Allah, and the decree stands for the Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the battlefield picture represent?
questions.answer: It represents this world, which is always changing and never stays the same.

questions.question: What question does a person begin to ask when seeing that worldly things pass away?
questions.answer: He wonders whether there is a way to keep things from being lost forever by turning them into something lasting.

questions.question: What answer does the Qur’an give to that worry?
questions.answer: It says there is an easy and beautiful way to do that.

questions.question: What is that way?
questions.answer: It is to return the trust to its true Owner by offering oneself and one’s property to Allah.

questions.question: What is the second profit?
questions.answer: Paradise is given as the reward.

questions.question: What is the main comparison being explained in this passage?
questions.answer: It explains human life and abilities through a parable about property being returned to its real owner.

questions.question: In this explanation, who is the true owner of everything a person has?
questions.answer: Allah is the true owner.

questions.question: Which parts of a human being are included among the trusts given by Allah?
questions.answer: The body, spirit, heart, senses, mind, and imagination are included.

questions.question: What role is given to the Messenger of Allah in the meaning of the parable?
questions.answer: He is the honored messenger who brings the call and guidance from Allah.

questions.question: Why is the world compared to a battlefield?
questions.answer: Because it is unstable, always changing, and full of loss and passing events.

questions.question: What human feeling leads a person to search for a lasting solution?
questions.answer: Seeing everything slip away makes a person want something permanent.

questions.question: What does it mean to sell the trust back to its true owner?
questions.answer: It means to use yourself and your possessions for Allah and according to His commands.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the result of giving one’s passing life to Allah?
questions.answer: That life becomes a source of everlasting reward.

questions.question: What reward is directly named as the price of this trade?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: Who is being addressed at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The human self that follows its desires is being addressed.

questions.question: What does the passage say our possessions really include, besides money and objects?
questions.answer: They include our inner and outer abilities, such as our senses, mind, heart, and soul.

questions.question: Why is the Qur’an connected to the decree in the parable?
questions.answer: Because it gives Allah’s command and explains the deal being offered to believers.

questions.question: What verse is referred to in the passage in a general sense?
questions.answer: It is the verse that says Allah takes the believers’ selves and wealth in exchange for Paradise.

questions.question: What idea is shown by the changing world around us?
questions.answer: It shows that earthly things do not last and cannot be held forever.

questions.question: What solution is offered to the problem of things passing away?
questions.answer: To dedicate what we have to Allah so it gains lasting value.

questions.question: Why is this trade called profitable?
questions.answer: Because it brings many benefits and saves a person from many losses.

questions.question: In the explained meaning of the parable, who is the ruler and who is the messenger?
questions.answer: The ruler is Allah, and the messenger is the Prophet of Allah.

questions.question: What do the human senses and inner abilities represent in the parable?
questions.answer: They are part of the trust placed in a person’s care during life.

questions.question: Why is life in this world described in terms of conflict and change?
questions.answer: Because everything in it keeps shifting, fading, and passing away.

questions.question: What important thought comes to a person who notices this constant change?
questions.answer: He thinks about how to keep what he has from being lost forever.

questions.question: What simple action is presented as the answer to this problem?
questions.answer: To hand the trust back to Allah by using it for Him.

questions.question: What is the better use of the eye?
questions.answer: To observe creation as signs of Allah’s wisdom and mercy.

questions.question: How can the tongue be either lowered or raised?
questions.answer: It is lowered when used only for appetite and raised when it becomes thankful for Allah’s provision.

questions.question: What makes the believer’s nature fit for Paradise?
questions.answer: Faith leads the believer to use Allah’s trust properly and within His limits.

questions.question: What is promised to those who worship Allah with their limbs and faculties?
questions.answer: They will receive a high reward in the form of the fruits of Paradise.

questions.question: What is the second loss of refusing the trade?
questions.answer: A person is punished for abusing what was entrusted to him.

questions.question: How is misusing human powers also an offense against Allah’s wisdom?
questions.answer: It drags noble human gifts down to a level lower than animals.

questions.question: What practice is taught at the end for someone who recognizes his shortcomings?
questions.answer: He should seek Allah’s forgiveness and ask to remain a faithful keeper of the trust.

questions.question: What truth is the passage trying to show by explaining the parable?
questions.answer: It is showing that our lives and abilities belong to Allah and should be used for Him.

questions.question: What are some examples of the inner and outer faculties mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: They include the eye, tongue, mind, imagination, heart, and spirit.

questions.question: What is the role of the Qur’an in this passage?
questions.answer: It announces and explains the deal between Allah and the believers.

questions.question: Why does the world make people worry about loss?
questions.answer: Because everything in it keeps changing and does not remain in human hands.

questions.question: What does the Qur’an offer as a hopeful answer to that worry?
questions.answer: It offers a way to turn passing things into lasting benefit.

questions.question: What does a person do when he sells the trust to Allah?
questions.answer: He uses his life, body, wealth, and abilities in obedience to Allah.

questions.question: What makes the first profit especially comforting?
questions.answer: It means the moments of life are not wasted but become everlasting reward.

questions.question: What is the second profit, stated simply?
questions.answer: Allah gives Paradise in return.

questions.question: In the passage, what happens to human faculties when they are used correctly?
questions.answer: They rise in value and serve a noble purpose.

questions.question: What happens when the mind is left to serve selfish desire?
questions.answer: It turns into a painful burden full of fear and sadness.

questions.question: What does the eye become when it is guided by Allah’s limits?
questions.answer: It becomes a way to read the signs of Allah in the world.

questions.question: What overall lesson should be learned from these examples?
questions.answer: Human abilities are meant to help a person worship Allah and reach eternal success.

questions.question: Why does the believer receive a higher value than the unbeliever in this discussion?
questions.answer: Because the believer is faithful with the trust, while the unbeliever misuses it.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about human weakness and need?
questions.answer: It teaches that people cannot carry life well without depending on Allah.

questions.question: What emotional harm comes from refusing to rely on Allah?
questions.answer: A person is left with heavy regret, pain, and inner unrest.

questions.question: How do people of spiritual understanding describe the reward of worship?
questions.answer: They say it will come as a great and elevated gift when it is most needed.

questions.question: What is one loss connected to loving worldly things too much?
questions.answer: They disappear and leave a burden of sin and pain behind.

questions.question: According to the ending of the passage, why is Allah’s path not too hard for people?
questions.answer: Because the lawful things are enough, and Allah’s commands are manageable and few.

questions.question: What is the passage teaching about ownership?
questions.answer: It teaches that what people have is really a trust from Allah, not something they own absolutely.

questions.question: Which human qualities and powers are included in that trust?
questions.answer: A person’s body, soul, heart, senses, intellect, and imagination are all included.

questions.question: In the explained parable, what do the messenger and the decree guide people toward?
questions.answer: They guide people toward giving themselves and their property to Allah in return for great reward.

questions.question: Why is the world described as stormy and unstable in meaning?
questions.answer: Because it keeps changing and causes people to realize that worldly things do not last.

questions.question: What deep question does that unstable condition create in a thoughtful person?
questions.answer: It makes him ask how temporary things can be preserved in a lasting way.

questions.question: What is the five-profit path mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: It is to return the trust to Allah by using it for His sake.

questions.question: How does this path change the value of a person’s life?
questions.answer: It turns a passing life into one that gives eternal fruit.

questions.question: What future reward is clearly named as part of this path?
questions.answer: Paradise is promised.

questions.question: What is the good use of the eye?
questions.answer: It is using the eye to witness Allah’s artistry and blessings.

questions.question: What is the difference between the low and high use of the tongue?
questions.answer: The low use is serving appetite only, while the high use is grateful recognition of Allah’s provision.

questions.question: What practical reason is given for putting trust in Allah?
questions.answer: Human beings are weak, needy, and unable to bear life’s hardships alone.

questions.question: Name one of the five losses of rejecting the trade.
questions.answer: One loss is that a person misuses precious gifts on worthless goals and harms himself.

questions.question: What final response should a believer have after learning this teaching?
questions.answer: He should serve Allah, stay within His law, ask forgiveness for mistakes, and pray to guard the trust well.
